t.6.91.1: Seeing the face of the wise Rāma, enraged, all beings trembled in terror, and the earth quaked.
t.6.91.3: And ominous birds, harsh-screeching and rough-voiced, circled all around in the sky, crying out loudly.
t.6.91.2: The mountain, home to lions and tigers, shook along with its trees, and the ocean too, lord of the rivers, was thrown into turmoil.
t.6.91.4: Seeing Rāma utterly enraged, and the most dreadful portents, all beings trembled with terror, and fear entered Rāvaṇa.
t.6.91.6: They then beheld the battle of the two heroes fighting fiercely with many kinds of terrible weapons, a battle that seemed like the dissolution of the worlds at the end of an age.
t.6.91.5: Then the gods standing in their celestial chariots, the Gandharvas and the great serpents, the Ṛṣis, Dānavas and Daityas, and the Garuḍas who range the sky.
t.6.91.7: Then all the gods and asuras, who had come to the battle and were watching that great combat, spoke these words with devotion, as if overjoyed.
t.6.91.8: The asuras, standing assembled there, said to Daśagrīva, "Be victorious!" And then the devas said to Rāma again and again, "May you be victorious!"
t.6.91.9: Meanwhile that evil-souled Rāvaṇa, wishing in his fury to strike Rāghava, grasped a mighty weapon.
t.6.91.10: Hard as the thunderbolt, mighty in its roar, the destroyer of all foes, studded with spikes like mountain peaks, it struck terror merely to behold.
t.6.91.11: It was sharp-pointed and seemed to smoke, like the massed fire at the end of the age, exceedingly terrible and unapproachable, hard to withstand even for Kāla himself.
t.6.91.12: Rāvaṇa, as if ablaze with fury, seized a spear that struck terror into all beings, one that could rend and pierce asunder.
t.6.91.13: Exceedingly enraged, the mighty one, surrounded in battle by many heroic rākṣasas, seized that spear by its middle.
t.6.91.15: Then the terrible sound of the lord of the rākṣasas made the earth and the sky, the cardinal directions and the intermediate directions tremble.
t.6.91.14: Raising his weapon aloft, the huge-bodied one, his eyes red with rage, roared terribly in battle, heartening his own army.
t.6.91.17: Having seized that great spear, the mighty Rāvaṇa let out a tremendous roar and spoke harsh words to Rāma.
t.6.91.16: At that roar of the evil-minded one, who roared tremendously, all creatures were terrified and the ocean was churned into turmoil.
t.6.91.18: O Rāma, this spear, hard as a thunderbolt, raised by me in fury against you, will at once take away the life of you who have your brother as your companion.
t.6.91.20: "Stand still now, O Rāghava! I shall slay you with this spear." Having spoken thus, the lord of the Rākṣasas hurled that spear.
t.6.91.19: Today, O you who boast of battle, I will slay you and swiftly make you like the heroic rākṣasas who have been slain at the head of the army.
t.6.91.21: Rāghava checked him as he rushed onward with a flood of arrows, just as Vāsava holds back with floods of water the fire of the world's end as it leaps upward.
t.6.91.22: That great spear of Rāvaṇa burned up those arrows released from Rāma's bow, as a fire burns up moths.
t.6.91.23: Seeing those arrows, still in the sky, crushed by the touch of the spear and reduced to ashes, Rāghava gave way to anger.
t.6.91.24: Exceedingly enraged, Rāghava, the delight of the Raghus, seized that spear fashioned by Vāsava and brought by Mātali.
t.6.91.25: That spear, brandished by the mighty one, its bells ringing out, lit up the sky, radiant like the meteor at the end of the age.
t.6.91.27: Then Rāma pierced his exceedingly swift horses with arrows, with sharp, whetted shafts of great velocity, like thunderbolts.
t.6.91.26: That spear, once hurled, fell upon that trident of the lord of the Rākṣasas, and the great trident, split apart by the spear, fell down, its splendor gone.
t.6.91.28: Then Rāghava, exerting himself to the utmost, pierced Rāvaṇa in the chest with sharpened arrows and in the forehead with three feathered shafts.
t.6.91.29: That lord of the Rākṣasas, all his limbs pierced by arrows and blood streaming from his body, standing amid his host, shone like an aśoka tree in full bloom.
t.6.91.30: That lord of the night-roamers, his body deeply pierced by Rāma's arrows and his limbs wet with blood, fell into distress in the midst of the assembly, and at that moment he flew into a most violent rage.
